:::{#def-data-splits}
#### Training/validation/test split

A **training/validation/test split** divides the observations $1, \ldots, N$ of a data set
into three disjoint sets of indices,
$I_{\text{train}}$, $I_{\text{val}}$ and $I_{\text{test}}$,
and takes the observations in $I_{\text{train}}$
as the [training set](#def-training-set):

$$
\ba
& I_{\text{train}} \cup I_{\text{val}} \cup I_{\text{test}} = \set{1, \ldots, N},
\\
& I_{\text{train}} \cap I_{\text{val}}
= I_{\text{train}} \cap I_{\text{test}}
= I_{\text{val}} \cap I_{\text{test}}
= \emptyset,
\\
& \trainset = \paren{(x_i, y_i)}_{i \in I_{\text{train}}}.
\ea
$$ {#eq-data-splits}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
#### Source

@james2021islr2e [pp. 198--201].
:::

:::

::: notes
In @exr-data-splits,
a rule of 60% / 20% / 20% on $N = 32$ cars
gives sets of 19, 6, and 7 cars,
and the 7 test cars are used only once, after the model is chosen.
:::
